title: The Last Time This Happened Was 1989 (3 Stocks Flashing Buy Signals)
creator: MarketBeat
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions
summary: MarketBeat hosts TradeSmith CEO Keith Kaplan after one of the wildest weeks in the market: the S&P 500 fell 4.36% in a single day on Thursday while within 2% of an all-time high — a pattern seen only twice in 70 years (September 1955 and October 1989) — then rebounded, with the CEO of the nation's largest tech company resigning in the same stretch. Kaplan argues the AI trade persists: roughly 82% of the S&P beat earnings, growth is running around 30%, hyperscalers are committing about $700bn this year, and memory remains the biggest choke point (Micron fell 17% in a day, which he calls a massive overreaction). His AI system scans about 2,500 stocks each morning for price-action 'fingerprints' and publishes a top-signals list; the Friday after the crash it fired 20 signals (AMD, Micron, Marvell, Lam Research, Cloudflare, Palantir among them), and 18 of 19 were higher by Wednesday morning, averaging about 18%. He then presents three live buy signals: Vertiv (VRT), a pivot signal after a 13%+14% two-day fall on politics with sales +61% and orders doubled; Rubrik (RBRK), a pivot signal after a 22% no-news crash-week fall, revenue +38%; and Palantir (PLTR), a sprint momentum signal after a near-10% fall to a 3-month low despite revenue +96% and guidance raised to ~$8.5bn. All three are short-term signal trades with system-set entries, exits and time stops (days to a month), not long-term investment cases. Kaplan closes with a Nasdaq 100 study: after a single-day fall of 6.35% or more since 2002, the index was up ~5.8% one month later (two times out of three), 12.7% in three months, 30.2% in six and 57.7% in twelve — higher every single time over two years. A free trial of the signals system and a live training event on Wednesday 18 November are promoted throughout.

calls.thesis: First tracked MarketBeat VRT call. Guest Keith Kaplan (TradeSmith CEO) flags a pivot (mean-reversion) signal on Vertiv, which builds data-centre power and cooling. Sales grew 61% last quarter and orders more than doubled; the stock then fell 13% one day and 14% the next on election/data-centre politics with nothing about the business changed. Short-term signal trade (system sets entry, exit target and a 1-month max hold), not a long-term investment case.
calls.base_case: Oversold snap-back: stock pushed too far too fast, history says it reverts; typical hold ~8 days.
calls.bull_case: Signal right 85.4% of the time over 158 occurrences, average return over 8%.

calls.thesis: BUY reiterated (was BUY). Guest Keith Kaplan (TradeSmith) flags a pivot signal on Rubrik, a cyber-recovery company (ransomware backup) that went public in 2024. Revenue grew 38% last quarter, recurring revenue north of $1.5bn; fell 22% in the crash week with no company news at all — sold off only because software was being sold. Short-term signal trade, typical hold ~6 days.
calls.base_case: Pivot snap-back after a no-news 22% sell-off; average return just under 5% in about 6 days.
calls.bear_case: Worst historical loss on this signal 14.9%.

calls.video_title: The Last Time This Happened Was 1989 (3 Stocks Flashing Buy Signals)
calls.thesis: FLIP from UNCERTAIN. Guest Keith Kaplan (TradeSmith) flags a sprint (momentum) signal on Palantir: AI platforms for governments and big companies. Revenue grew 96% last quarter, US commercial +148%, full-year guidance raised to about $8.5bn; stock still fell almost 10% on Thursday to a 3-month low. Momentum name on a pullback — already moving, history says it keeps moving. Short-term signal trade, about a week.
calls.base_case: Momentum continuation after the pullback; average return almost 7% in about a week.
calls.bull_case: Highest win rate on the list: right over 93% of the time (61 occurrences).
calls.bear_case: Only 61 occurrences (smaller sample than the other two) and valuation makes Palantir speculative by any measure — it moves fast both ways, so size it smaller.
